arxiv-2305-09157.title: Weak gravitational lensing and shadow cast by rotating black holes in axionic Chern-Simons theory
arxiv-2305-09157.creator: Nashiba Parbin, Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, Umananda Dev Goswami
arxiv-2305-09157.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Nashiba Parbin, Dhruba Jyoti Gogoi, Umananda Dev Goswami. We investigate the impact of the axionic coupling parameter on the bending angle of light and the shadow cast by slowly rotating black holes in Chern-Simons modified gravity. pmc-11322651.description: Real-time and accurate biomarker detection is highly desired in point-of-care diagnosis, food freshness monitoring, and hazardous leakage warning. pmc-11492745.description: BackgroundChildren spend a significant amount of time engaging in sedentary behaviors, defined as activities that do not increase energy expenditure significantly above resting levels, such as watching TV and playing PC/video games. pmc-12397348.creator: Arsalan Mahmoodzadeh, Hamid Reza Nejati, Nejib Ghazouani, Abdulaziz Alghamdi
pmc-12397348.description: This study examines the intricate task of predicting construction duration for drill-and-blast tunnels utilizing machine learning (ML) techniques. First, a comprehensive dataset (500 data points) encompassing 20 diverse parameters was compiled by constructing eight tunnels. After meticulous analysis, 17 of the 20 parameters were identified as crucial for training the algorithms.

pmc-12604800.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundLittle is known about public perceptions of antivirals for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in the United States (US). Our objective was to explore adult perceptions toward COVID-19 antivirals to improve outreach communications about antivirals for COVID-19.MethodsDuring July 2022, potential respondents ≥18 years were randomly sampled from a national opt-in internet panel, with oversampling of African Americans, Hispanics, and adults ≥65 years. Respondents were asked about sociodemographic factors, and knowledge, attitudes, and perceptions regarding COVID-19 antivirals.

uslaw-usc-t49-s80116.title: 49 U.S.C. § 80116 — Criminal penalty
uslaw-usc-t49-s80116.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t49-s80116.description: United States Code, Title 49 (Transportation); Chapter 801 (Bills Of Lading). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. A person shall be fined under title 18, imprisoned for not more than 5 years, or both, if the person— (1) violates this chapter with intent to defraud; or (2) knowingly or with intent to defraud— (A) falsely makes, alters, or copies a bill of lading.
